notes: SCENARIO RATE FIELDS COULD NOT BE EDITED. The previous attempt (v2026.05.09.03) blamed the in-app numpad and did not fix it; the real cause was elsewhere. ACTUAL CAUSE: _calcPromote rewrites any numeric input to type=text the moment it receives focus, so that arithmetic expressions such as 1.1+2.2 can be typed. Two consequences followed. The up and down arrows disappeared, because a text input has no spinner. And readScenarioEditFields gated its percent-to-decimal conversion on input.type === 'number' — a test that is FALSE by the time the field has been focused and edited. The conversion was therefore skipped, and the raw string was written under the wrong key, so assetGrowth never changed and the edit appeared to do nothing. THE SAME DEFECT AFFECTED LOAN RATE, and had done since that field existed: focus it, change it to 9.25, and 9.25 was stored where 0.0925 belonged — a 925% loan. Any scenario whose rate was edited after focusing the field has been wrong. Worth re-checking existing scenarios after loading this build. FIXED IN TWO PLACES. First, numeric handling in readScenarioEditFields no longer tests input.type, which is rewritten underneath it; it checks the calc-ready flag and inputmode as well, so a promoted field is still recognised as numeric. This also means money fields now store as numbers rather than strings once promoted, which they did not before. Second, a data-plain-number opt-out lets small pre-filled numbers such as interest rates skip both the calculator promotion and the numpad, keeping type=number and its arrows. VERIFIED AFTER FOCUSING THE FIELD, which is what previously failed: growth 8 stores 0.08 and redisplays as 8.0; loan rate 9.25 stores 0.0925 and redisplays as 9.25; the arrows step; and the clamping from the previous build still holds, so 800 becomes 30% rather than 800%. Confirmed no regression to the calculator: normal money fields are still promoted, 1.1+2.2 still evaluates to 3.3, and an edited cost stores as the number 12000000. LESSON WORTH RECORDING: reading a DOM property that another feature mutates at runtime is a silent-failure pattern. The type check looked correct in isolation and was correct until the field was focused. Intent should be read from a stable attribute set by the author, not from live state another handler can rewrite. Regression confirms the Projection-to-Dashboard and Decisions-to-chain gaps both remain zero. No page errors.
